name: Sarua
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only comparative/classificatory refs surfaced (Jungraithmayr 1977; Jungraithmayr & Peust 2021); no grammar or phonology of Sarua located

tone_statements.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Carsten Peust. 2021. A Sketch of Sarwa, a Chadic Minority Language in Central Chad. Zeitschrift der Deutschen Morgenländischen Gesellschaft 171(1): 9-37.
tone_statements.quote: Sarwa is a three tone level language:5 à low, ā mid, á high. In addition, various contour tones exist, such as â high–low, a᷄ mid–high, a᷆ mid–low, e. g. ndû “locust”, nàrâ “persons”, ndǝ̀mâ “sheep”, nju᷄ “goat”, ŋgīrīm̀ “crocodile”. [fn. 5:] Abderamane Abdoul (2016, p. 32) recognizes only two tone levels for Sarwa. But tone was evidently not in the focus of his research, so that various inconsistencies of tone appear among multiple quotations of the same word in his work. [...] [p. 36:] in its tonal equipment, the two level outfit typical of the east has already increased to a three level system.
tone_statements.locator: p. 11, section 2.3 'Tones' with footnote 5; final clause from p. 36, section 4 conclusion; verbal tone classes at section 3.4.6, pp. 28-29
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 level (L, M, H) + contour HL, MH, ML; verbal tone classes M-HL, H-HL, L-L

sources.citation: Abdoul, Djimé Abderamane. 2023. Essai phonologique du sarwa, langue en danger, langue tchadique de Bousso (Tchad). Akofena n°009, vol. 3: 283-294. DOI 10.48734/akofena.n009v3-24.2023
sources.note: Nothing. Segmental inventory only (26 consonants, 9 short + 7 long vowels), explicitly 'en nous limitant sur les voyelles et les consonnes'. All data are tone-marked; the only suprasegmental remark (p. 287): 'Dans le contexte de voyelles longues ayant un même ton (isotone), le ton de la seconde voyelle se reporte sur la première voyelle.' No mention of accent/stress.

sources.citation: Abdoul, Djimé Abderamane. 2023. Le système verbal du sarwa, langue tchadique du Loug-Chari, Tchad. Akofena Varia n°10, vol. 2: 465-474. DOI 10.48734/akofena.s010-41.2023
sources.note: Nothing; verb morphology (ablaut classes, nd- infinitive prefix), syllable types of verb stems; tone-marked data; no prosody discussion.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Carsten Peust. 2019. Notes on Gàlì (Miltu), a moribund Chadic language (Republic of Chad). Folia Orientalia 56: 219-230.
sources.note: About neighbouring Gali (Miltu), not Sarwa; mentions Sarwa only as the western neighbour belonging to the Sumray subgroup of East Chadic A. Nothing on Sarwa prosody.

sources.citation: Peust, Carsten. 2018. The subgrouping of East Chadic. Folia Orientalia 55: 235-253.
sources.note: Lexical-innovation subgrouping of 16 East Chadic languages; Sarwa is not among them and is not mentioned.

sources.note: The only published grammatical sketch by professional Chadicists; abstract promises 'a brief overview of the phonology' (tone and possibly accent) before the morphology; Peust's companion sketches (Gali 2019, Gadang 2022, West Dangla 2014) each have an explicit tone/prosody subsection, so this is the most likely place for a stress/tone statement.

tone.says: First-hand tone statement (section 2.3 'Tones', p. 11): Sarwa has three level tones -- low (à), mid (ā), high (á) -- plus contour tones HL, MH, ML (e.g. ndû 'locust', nju᷄ 'goat'); footnote 5 notes that Abderamane Abdoul 2016 (p. 32) recognized only two tone levels but calls his tone notation inconsistent.
